question.text: Yamuna Credit AIF (Category II) is raising capital from a Mauritius-based family office. Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations and the Oct 2024 SEBI circular, which check must the Manager perform before onboarding this foreign investor?

answer.text: Confirm that the investor's home-country regulator is IOSCO MMoU Appendix-A signatory or has bilateral MoU with SEBI, and verify the investor/BO is NOT on UNSC sanctions list or from FATF high-risk jurisdictions
Only a PAN card and bank statement; no home-country regulator check needed
Confirm the investor is a US-resident QIB
Confirm the investor holds a valid Indian GST registration

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI Circular dated Dec 9, 2022 (and Jan 11, 2024) requires that foreign investors in AIFs are residents of a country whose securities market regulator is an IOSCO MMoU (Appendix-A) signatory OR has a bilateral MoU with SEBI. Additionally, the investor or its beneficial owner shall NOT be: (a) on the UNSC Sanctions List, or (b) resident in a FATF high-risk jurisdiction under counter-measures. Existing investors failing these conditions cannot have further drawdowns. The 2024 land-border amendment adds extra diligence for Chinese/other land-border countries. The Trap: Option B trivialises the due-diligence requirement. Option C confines to US QIBs which is an ICDR concept, not foreign-investor onboarding. Option D is irrelevant (GST applies to services, not LP onboarding). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-B Distributor also test foreign-investor onboarding. XXIV AML tests the FATF/UNSC sanctions framework. X-A/B Investment Adviser exams include FEMA foreign-client onboarding. Manager's Pro-Tip: Maintain a 'foreign-LP matrix' per investor: (i) home regulator + IOSCO status, (ii) FATF risk rating of jurisdiction, (iii) UBO screening against UNSC/OFAC/EU sanctions, (iv) annual refresh. Any LP from Mauritius/Cayman/Singapore is routinely questioned by SEBI in inspections — maintain comprehensive BO trail.
